findings.title: [P1] Parse `cached.value`, not the metadata wrapper, on cache hit
findings.body: `Cache.get` now returns `{ value: string; stale: boolean } | null` (`src/cache.ts:6-8`), but `loadProfile` still calls `JSON.parse(cached)` on the result. For every non-null cache hit, `cached` is the wrapper object: `JSON.parse` coerces it to `"[object Object]"` and throws `SyntaxError` (and the call is a TypeScript type error, since `JSON.parse` requires `string`). The base code was self-consistent (`string | null` parsed directly), so this break is introduced by this PR. Any profile present in the cache fails to load; only cache misses work. Fix: `return JSON.parse(cached.value);` (and decide how the `stale` flag should be handled).

findings.title: [P3] Empty-string cache values now throw instead of falling back to the API
findings.body: The old truthy check (`if (cached)`) treated an empty cached string as a miss and fell through to `api.loadProfile`; the new `cached === null` check treats it as a hit, so `JSON.parse("")` throws `SyntaxError` even after the P1 fix. Only bites if the store can return an empty `value`; worth confirming that can't happen or guarding it.
